title: The $110 Billion Deal That Would Merge Marvel, Star Wars, Harry Potter, DC, and HBO Into One Company Is About to Be Approved
excerpt: US antitrust regulators are reportedly set to clear Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. Hollywood stars are fighting it. The Indian streaming market — Paramount's fastest-growing — is watching.
body:
The United States Department of Justice is reportedly on the verge of approving Paramount's $110 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, a deal that would create the largest entertainment conglomerate in history and fundamentally reshape the streaming landscape that hundreds of millions of Indians use every day.

## What the Deal Combines

Under one corporate roof, the merged entity would control: **Paramount Pictures** (Mission: Impossible, Top Gun, Transformers), **Marvel Studios and Lucasfilm** (through Paramount's parent company's existing arrangements), **Warner Bros. Pictures** (Harry Potter, The Matrix, Dune), **DC Studios** (Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman), **HBO** (Game of Thrones, Succession, The Last of Us), **CNN**, **Discovery Channel**, **Paramount+**, and **Max** (formerly HBO Max).

The deal, led by Paramount CEO David Ellison, received shareholder approval in April. The remaining hurdle was antitrust clearance from the Justice Department, which Semafor reported is now expected to be granted following a recent meeting.

## The Opposition

The approval has not come quietly. Some of Hollywood's biggest names — including Jane Fonda, J.J. Abrams, and Mark Ruffalo — have publicly opposed the merger, arguing it would lead to fewer opportunities for writers, directors, and actors, accelerate job losses across the industry, and ultimately raise prices for consumers.

Their argument is straightforward: when fewer companies control more content, the people who create that content lose leverage. The entertainment industry has already shed tens of thousands of jobs since the streaming wars began, and a Paramount-Warner merger would give the combined company enormous power to set terms across the entire value chain — from talent deals to theater distribution to streaming pricing.

## The India Market

India is where this merger gets personal for the diaspora. Warner Bros. Discovery's streaming platforms and Paramount+ have been aggressively expanding in the Indian market, competing with Disney+ Hotstar, Netflix, and Amazon Prime Video for the attention of 400 million potential streaming subscribers.

The combined company would control an enormous library of content — both Western and localized Indian productions — and would have the scale to compete directly with Reliance-Disney's merged JioCinema-Hotstar platform, which currently dominates Indian streaming after its own mega-merger in 2024.

For Indian consumers and the diaspora, the practical question is whether consolidation leads to better content at fair prices, or fewer choices at higher costs. The track record of media mergers suggests the latter, but the companies involved have argued that scale is the only way to survive in a market where Netflix and YouTube still command the most hours of attention.

## The Streaming Math

The numbers tell the story of why this deal exists. Paramount+ has roughly 72 million global subscribers. Max has about 110 million. Combined, the merged service would have around 180 million subscribers — still behind Netflix's 310 million but large enough to compete for second place globally.

For India specifically, the merged company would have the resources to invest in original Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu-language content at a scale that neither Paramount nor Warner could afford independently. Whether they choose to do so is another question entirely.

## What Happens Next

If the DOJ formally approves — which could happen within days — Paramount has structured the deal to close quickly, offering a quarterly "ticking fee" to Warner Bros. shareholders if the transaction is not completed by October. That urgency suggests Ellison wants the integration underway before the next awards season and well ahead of the 2027 content slate.

For the Indian entertainment market and the diaspora that straddles both Hollywood and Bollywood, this merger is not just a business story. It is a structural shift in who controls the stories that reach 1.4 billion people — and the 30 million in the diaspora who watch both worlds.
